lines.description: The requested lines. An order must have at least one.

sku.description: The stock keeping unit ordered. Must be non-empty.

quantity.description: Quantity ordered. Must be greater than zero. int64, not int32: the service is a 64-bit Go binary whose quantity validation is "greater than zero" only, so it genuinely accepts (and echoes) quantities beyond 2^31-1 — this spec documents that reality.

giftWrap.description: OPTIONAL. Whether the requester asked the warehouse to produce a gift package for this line. Passed straight through onto the enriched `OrderAllocated`/`OrderPartiallyAllocated` Kafka event's `lines[].gift_wrap` field — a caller-stated characteristic, never looked up.

requiredShipBy.description:
OPTIONAL. An externally-dictated deadline (RFC 3339) — the instant this order must ship by, set by someone other than this service (a retail network's required ship-by, for example).

When present the promise is CONSTRAINED to a CPT window at or before it, rather than being the earliest window this service can manage; specifically, the LATEST window that still meets the deadline is chosen, leaving the floor maximum slack (ADR 0020 §2). When the deadline cannot be met the order is still created and allocated, but comes back with NO `promiseDate` at all — an absent promise is the honest signal that we cannot commit, and is exactly what a caller holding a fill-or-kill obligation needs to see before acknowledging it downstream.

Unlike the ordinary promise path, this one has NO lead-time fallback: missing schedule or capability data yields no promise rather than an estimate, because a guess dressed as a commitment is worse than an admission of ignorance.

releaseOnAllocation.description: When true (the default, and the behaviour of every caller that omits the field), the order is received, allocated and released in one call exactly as before ADR 0020. When false the order is HELD: lines are allocated, inventory reservations genuinely exist and a promise is computed and attached, but nothing is released and no work reaches the floor until `POST /orders/{id}/release`. Intended for a caller that must decide whether to commit to the order before it becomes work — see ADR 0020. A held order must be ship-complete: sending `releaseOnAllocation: false` together with `allowPartialShipment: true` is rejected with `422`.

allowPartialShipment.description: When false (the default — ship-complete, BR3), a single backordered line holds the WHOLE order back from release until retry-allocation clears it. When true, allocated lines are independently eligible for release.
